title: Health-First Systems
hook: Walking into a big sales call already wired and tense rarely ends well.
statement: Calm your nervous system first, then do the hard task.
explainer: Stress narrows your focus and makes your judgment worse, even when you know your stuff. Ninety seconds of settling down before a big task often beats more prep.
sop: Build one daily calming habit before email: breathwork, a walk, movement.
Do a 60-second body check before high-stakes work: breath, jaw, shoulders.
Rate your Nervous System Balance 1 to 10 before your top priority.
Do a quick reset the moment you feel stress spike.
Keep the habits that work for you. Drop the rest.
equation_example: Nothing to multiply here, just a scale. Rate yourself 1 to 10 before a task. At a 3, decisions and output drop. At an 8, the same task goes faster with fewer mistakes. Higher means clearer thinking. Lower means your skills are harder to reach.
question: Write down the one thing you'll do to calm down before your next big task.
closing_statement: A calm nervous system beats a motivated one.
caption:
Principle Nº 216: Health-First Systems
